milestones.title: Truthful architecture narrative
milestones.outcome: Separate live architecture, target architecture, decisions and measured benchmarks.

milestones.title: Verified artifact publication
milestones.outcome: A pinned trust root verifies a signed manifest for every served artifact.

milestones.title: Expandable temporal EU corpus
milestones.outcome: Configuration selects domains while every accepted work retains all official dated expressions.

milestones.title: Deduplicated index
milestones.outcome: lex-index/3 stores repeated wording once without changing timelines, exact text or diffs.

milestones.title: Local hybrid retrieval
milestones.outcome: Keyword and local semantic retrieval fuse deterministically only after the public quality gate passes.

milestones.title: Lawyer-facing scope filters
milestones.outcome: Jurisdiction, hierarchy, legal form, binding status, domain, language and date remain explicit.

milestones.title: Luxembourg original-act expansion
milestones.outcome: Add reviewed normative acts outside the Legilux consolidation catalogue with document-class-specific temporal semantics.

milestones.title: Size-gated local index hosting
milestones.outcome: Small verified indexes run locally in Container Apps. Oversized releases remain deployment-blocked until the zero-traffic VM-managed local-disk path is implemented and measured.

milestones.title: Reviewed search enrichment and legal-research agent
milestones.outcome: Publisher metadata, reviewed aliases, deterministic work resolution, bounded retrieval, Agent Framework evidence composition and judging, bounded memory and jurisdiction-first results are live without changing authoritative legal text. Model-derived weak discovery remains excluded from production retrieval.

decisions.title: Select binding acts, then close legal relationships
decisions.choice: Use reviewed domain configuration and bounded legal-history relationships.
decisions.alternative: Ingest roughly 59,100 works selected only by broad subject codes.
decisions.reason: A lawyer needs complete context for selected law, not a large shelf with arbitrary gaps.
decisions.cost: Selection rules and relationship traversal require review and dry-run reporting.

decisions.title: Store repeated wording once
decisions.choice: Map every dated occurrence to a content-addressed text state.
decisions.alternative: Store and embed every repeated provision occurrence.
decisions.reason: The timeline is preserved while index size, vector size and duplicate hits fall.
decisions.cost: The reader must reconstruct a version through occurrence mappings.

decisions.title: Run semantic retrieval locally
decisions.choice: Use a pinned local embedding encoder, compact vectors and fixed rank fusion.
decisions.alternative: Buy Azure AI Search for the current corpus and traffic.
decisions.reason: Local retrieval preserves deterministic behavior and avoids a fixed managed-search bill.
decisions.cost: Lex owns model packaging, vector indexing and relevance evaluation.

decisions.title: Move the host when the measured index outgrows the image
decisions.choice: Keep query files local: use Container Apps for a small verified set, and promote releases above the recorded size or runtime gates from Blob onto a VM-managed disk.
decisions.alternative: Commit permanently to either Container Apps, a VM, Blob range reads or an Azure Files-mounted SQLite database regardless of measurements.
decisions.reason: Blob is the durable distribution layer, while SQLite FTS and memory-mapped vectors require local random access. The completed artifact, rollback footprint and runtime gates determine the cheapest correct host.
decisions.cost: The pipeline blocks releases that exceed the active Container Apps path. A second verified VM deployment path and operating-system patching remain to be implemented before such a release can receive traffic.

decisions.title: Represent hierarchy as metadata
decisions.choice: Store legal hierarchy and domain fields beside each work and state.
decisions.alternative: Create a separate database for every legal level.
decisions.reason: Hierarchy is a query filter, while physical boundaries should follow provenance and update behavior.
decisions.cost: The ingestion model must normalize publisher classifications without erasing them.

decisions.title: Never synthesize consolidation
decisions.choice: Show official text and amendment events, and name a missing consolidation explicitly.
decisions.alternative: Mechanically apply amendments and present the result as current law.
decisions.reason: A plausible unofficial merge would violate the product's evidence claim.
decisions.cost: Some works remain metadata and timeline only until the publisher supplies consolidated wording.

decisions.title: Pin trust outside the artifact
decisions.choice: Verify a whole-artifact manifest with a public-key fingerprint pinned in the release.
decisions.alternative: Trust the public key stored beside its signature in the same database.
decisions.reason: Replacing an artifact must not let an attacker replace its trust root too.
decisions.cost: Key rotation becomes an explicit dual-trust release.

decisions.title: Use fuzzy matching only as fallback
decisions.choice: Expand ordinary terms only when exact lexical retrieval is weak and show every expansion.
decisions.alternative: Apply fuzzy expansion to every query.
decisions.reason: Legal identifiers, quotations and exact terms must not acquire silent near-matches.
decisions.cost: Some misspellings wait for the exact pass to return before expansion.

decisions.title: Publish claims only with evidence
decisions.choice: Separate live facts, target state, decisions and reproducible benchmarks.
decisions.alternative: Mix roadmap claims and hand-written benchmark numbers into one architecture page.
decisions.reason: An interviewer or lawyer must be able to distinguish what exists from what is proposed.
decisions.cost: Every public metric carries commits, artifact identity, environment and review status.

decisions.title: Export transparent reading aids
decisions.choice: Build citations and Markdown evidence from the exact structured article or comparison already on screen.
decisions.alternative: Generate a polished PDF or fetch and compare the law again during export.
decisions.reason: Lawyers can move traceable text into their work without a second result disagreeing or an unofficial file resembling a publisher document.
decisions.cost: Markdown prioritizes inspectable provenance over print-perfect presentation and remains explicitly a reading aid.

decisions.title: Keep one temporal research workspace
decisions.choice: Keep search, dated reading, version history and comparison in one URL-addressable workspace with stable legal context.
decisions.alternative: Split search, reading and comparison into separate products, or make a chatbot the primary navigation model.
decisions.reason: Lawyers need to see jurisdiction, applicable date, source and comparison state while moving between discovery and verification.
decisions.cost: The workspace is denser than a simple search page, so smaller screens require progressive disclosure and deliberate control grouping.

decisions.title: Expand Luxembourg by normative document class
decisions.choice: Implement and review original-act semantics per admitted Legilux document class.
decisions.alternative: Ingest every resource labelled Act as if it had consolidation semantics.
decisions.reason: The broad Act catalogue mixes lawyer-relevant rules with notices and records whose dates and manifestations mean different things.
decisions.cost: The first increment needs a new adapter, fixtures, scope preview and retrieval tests before later form additions become configuration-led.

decisions.title: Drive search facets from mounted indexes
decisions.choice: Build jurisdiction, hierarchy, domain, form, status and language controls from values in verified mounted indexes.
decisions.alternative: Maintain a second hard-coded list of supported scopes in the web client.
decisions.reason: A reviewed domain or jurisdiction must become searchable without an unrelated React implementation change.
decisions.cost: Friendly labels use stable overrides for known legal vocabulary and a deterministic fallback for new values.

decisions.title: Make semantic indexing bounded and deterministic
decisions.choice: Choose legal chunk boundaries first, then embed first-seen unique chunks in bounded batches with item-level progress and resumable compatible results.
decisions.alternative: Copy a whole remaining annex for every chunk, let hardware shape legal boundaries, or publish partial vector shards.
decisions.reason: Large annexes must finish within a predictable memory and time budget without changing the text, chunk order, citations or final vector ordinals.
decisions.cost: Batch and cache settings become stamped build configuration, and an incompatible model, tokenizer, vector format or runtime deliberately invalidates reuse.

decisions.title: Own legal semantics, reuse commodity engines
decisions.choice: Keep temporal selection, legal provenance, consolidation refusals, hierarchy filtering and authoritative provision mapping in Lex, while delegating keyword scoring, model inference, tokenization, document parsing and cryptographic primitives to maintained libraries.
decisions.alternative: Either implement general-purpose search and machine-learning engines inside Lex, or outsource the complete legal index to a managed search service.
decisions.reason: Libraries can optimize generic computation, but they do not know which official wording applied on a date or when Lex must refuse an unsupported consolidation claim.
decisions.cost: Lex maintains small integration layers and benchmarks replacement engines; commodity boundaries are migrated only when parity, artifact reproducibility and operational cost are measured.

decisions.title: Use the official MCP SDK without a premature service split
decisions.choice: Keep legal tools in the transport-neutral Lex.Mcp library, host local stdio in Lex.Mcp.Stdio, and compose the official Streamable HTTP adapter into the existing web runtime.
decisions.alternative: Maintain handwritten JSON-RPC transports or deploy an otherwise identical MCP-only Container App behind a proxy.
decisions.reason: The official SDK owns protocol negotiation and framing. HTTP MCP and the site consume the same indexes, scale together and have no distinct security or availability boundary, so a second runtime would duplicate memory, artifacts, cold starts and failure modes without isolating a real workload.
decisions.cost: MCP and web revisions are promoted together today. Extract the HTTP host only when measured traffic requires independent scaling, releases, tenant isolation or an SLA; the library boundary makes that move mechanical.

decisions.title: Delegate only the generic visual diff algorithm
decisions.choice: Use DiffPlex for the bounded line-diff shown after Lex has selected and aligned comparable legal text.
decisions.alternative: Maintain a quadratic handwritten LCS matrix or delegate the legal comparison workflow to a generic text-diff library.
decisions.reason: DiffPlex removes commodity algorithm code and quadratic memory while Lex retains the temporal and legal correctness boundary.
decisions.cost: Lex keeps output caps, escaping and compatibility tests, and must continue auditing the dependency; DiffPlex does not decide whether two legal provisions are comparable.

decisions.title: Make semantic builds portable and resumable
decisions.choice: Run the same deterministic index writer on CPU or a reviewed local DirectML GPU, record the runtime/provider, and cache compatible quantized vectors by chunk hash and complete embedding profile.
decisions.alternative: Recompute every vector on each ephemeral Fleet run, publish partial shards, or require the serving host to perform ingestion.
decisions.reason: A 770,450-chunk first backfill exceeds the free runner window, while content-addressed results are independently reusable without changing legal text, chunk order or final vector ordinals.
decisions.cost: The build cache is additional private evidence to retain and validate; provider changes intentionally invalidate it, and every final artifact still requires benchmarks and signed-manifest promotion.

decisions.title: Stabilize GPU tensor shapes after legal chunking
decisions.choice: Select authoritative provision and paragraph chunk boundaries first, then group the immutable chunks into 32/64/128/256/512-token inference buckets with masked transient padding.
decisions.alternative: Compile a new DirectML graph shape for each batch maximum, pad every chunk to 512 tokens, or change legal chunk boundaries to fit the GPU.
decisions.reason: Variable tensor shapes caused repeated DirectML graph preparation and an unbounded backfill ETA. A few fixed shapes retain the exact text and reduce compilation churn without paying maximum-sequence compute for every short provision.
decisions.cost: Bucket order becomes part of the deterministic embedding profile and cache identity. The build may have one partially filled batch per bucket, and every shape-policy change intentionally invalidates the embedding cache.

decisions.title: Fuse jurisdictions without comparing incomparable scores
decisions.choice: Rank each publisher locally, then combine eligible Luxembourg and EU results with deterministic reciprocal-rank fusion while retaining provenance.
decisions.alternative: Concatenate indexes or compare raw BM25 and vector scores produced by different publisher corpora.
decisions.reason: A single lawyer-facing result list needs both jurisdictions, but raw relevance scores are not calibrated across independently built indexes.
decisions.cost: Cross-publisher ordering is rank-based rather than a global score, and exact duplicate hits must be collapsed before presentation.

decisions.title: Keep publisher time semantics explicit
decisions.choice: Label Legilux applicability intervals as legal applicability, and EUR-Lex consolidated-expression dates as official publisher wording states across the workspace, exports, canonical pages and MCP envelopes.
decisions.alternative: Call every open-ended version interval ‘in force’ because both publishers expose dated version histories.
decisions.reason: A consolidation dated 2016 for an EU regulation can predate its application. Calling that date entry into force would turn a correct publisher timeline into legally misleading UI and structured metadata.
decisions.cost: Every new publisher must declare its timeline semantics. Older EUR-Lex artifacts need a narrow compatibility fallback until the next signed rebuild.

decisions.title: Recover official text without weakening provenance
decisions.choice: Add immutable fallback profiles that verify the requested act before deriving an official AKN body, older gazette article typography, or one document when the official section has no unambiguous single article sequence.
decisions.alternative: Broaden the existing published profiles, OCR every PDF, or attach the first readable legal text in a linked gazette issue.
decisions.reason: Coverage is useful only when each recovered word still belongs to the requested official instrument and the extraction confidence remains visible.
decisions.cost: A confirmed publisher source mismatch remains wordless, profile boundaries may block visual comparison, and every new document shape needs a regression fixture plus full-corpus validation.

decisions.title: Bound GPU batches by padded-token cost
decisions.choice: Keep the reviewed item batch as an upper bound and cap each fixed-shape inference call at 32,768 padded tokens.
decisions.alternative: Use one item count for every token bucket, lower all batches to the longest bucket's limit, or retry opaque out-of-memory failures manually.
decisions.reason: A batch that is efficient for 32-token provisions can exhaust an 8 GB DirectML worker in the longest bucket even though every legal chunk and model is valid.
decisions.cost: Long buckets use more inference calls, the token budget becomes stamped build configuration, and hardware-specific tuning must remain a transient grouping concern rather than changing legal chunks.

decisions.title: Separate authoritative text from provenance-aware search enrichment
decisions.choice: Build a publisher-first work catalog from official identifiers, titles, short titles and classifications, plus reviewed collision-aware aliases. Store accepted model-derived concepts in a quarantined trust class and activate them only if a separate held-out ablation proves incremental value without ranking or latency regressions. Any work vectors share the existing signed vector artifact through typed SQLite ordinal mappings.
decisions.alternative: Treat generated metadata as legal fact or a strong rank signal, maintain a runtime sidecar database, repeat work metadata inside every provision vector, or keep professional names in application code.
decisions.reason: Professional names require deterministic publisher metadata and reviewed overrides, while descriptive discovery requires candidate retrieval without silently converting a repeated model output into authority. A single verified artifact keeps provenance and rollback atomic.
decisions.cost: Publisher metadata retention, alias collision handling, proposal provenance, evidence anchors, separate legal and enrichment digests, typed ordinal validation, clean corpus migration and independent regression benchmarks become build responsibilities.

decisions.title: Keep retrieval authority deterministic and use Agent Framework for grounded composition
decisions.choice: Resolve the raw user query and authorize work-specific tools in application code, run a bounded tool-calling retrieval loop over the shared MCP core, then use Agent Framework for claim-typed evidence composition and the conditional grounding judge.
decisions.alternative: Give a model authority over work identity and citations, make the chatbot the primary navigator, or introduce a hierarchy of peer research agents.
decisions.reason: Exact lookup and tool permission must not become stochastic, while synthesized prose benefits from structured composition and an independent evidence check.
decisions.cost: The bounded retrieval loop and Framework composer/judge add model latency, tokens, session/privacy handling and evaluation work. The planner is application-hosted rather than a single Agent Framework research agent.

decisions.title: Partition results by jurisdiction and keep overlapping dimensions as facets
decisions.choice: Show Luxembourg and EU result sections, nest matching passages under each law, and scope hierarchy, practice area, class, form, status and language controls to the selected jurisdiction.
decisions.alternative: Interleave every publisher result without a source partition, or group by overlapping practice areas and duplicate the same work across categories.
decisions.reason: Jurisdiction is a disjoint provenance boundary; the other legal dimensions overlap and are clearer as filters than as competing result taxonomies.
decisions.cost: The search response/UI need per-jurisdiction counts, dependent facet handling, accessible disclosure and responsive regression tests.

baseline.note: Application Insights aggregates describe the current service, not the future hybrid retrieval path.
